episode_title: Turning Brand Messaging Into a Strategic Advantage with Tamsen Webster of Message Design Institute

real_qa.q: What is the difference between message design and storytelling in B2B marketing?
real_qa.r: Message design and storytelling are related but not the same. A story sits on top of a message, and message design helps find the foundation under which storytelling and content build. Message design is about making sure there is something clearly agreeable about the underlying idea, whereas storytelling is how you construct and illustrate that idea. If the foundation is not strong—if people do not understand it or agree with it—then how beautifully told the story is will not matter.

real_qa.q: Why do mission statements fail to capture what a company actually does?
real_qa.r: Mission statements tend to be aspirational and future-focused rather than describing what is actually happening right now. This creates a disconnect when marketing language infected by aspirational mission statements does not match the lived experience of customers. Message design should excavate what is actually true about an organization through a five whys exercise, not invent what the company wishes were true, because telling the truth is important for building trust and long-term relationships.
real_qa.requete: why mission statements do not work marketing

real_qa.q: How should B2B companies identify their core message when rethinking brand messaging?
real_qa.r: Start by identifying what question your ideal audience already wants answered—not the problem they have but the want they already feel. Then determine two and only two overlooked or underappreciated elements that answer that want. For example, if your audience wants better visibility into social selling results, you might identify comprehensiveness and consistent reporting framework as the two elements your solution provides. Build the argument using beliefs your audience already holds, rather than trying to convince them of new ones.
real_qa.requete: how to identify core message B2B strategy

real_qa.q: What does Tamsen Webster mean by values in use versus professed values?
real_qa.r: Values in use are what an organization actually prioritizes in practice, often revealed through real behavior and experience. Professed values are what the organization says it believes. United Airlines professes 'fly the friendly skies' but their values in use are actually maximizing shareholder value or prioritizing business flyers, creating a disconnect between what the brand says and what most customers actually experience.
real_qa.requete: values in use definition company alignment

real_qa.q: What is the three-stage process for turning message design into content?
real_qa.r: The first stage is the foundation—identifying the core idea and what action you want the audience to take. The second stage is framing—determining the architecture, examples, case studies, evidence, and third-party validation needed to make the message understandable and representative. The third stage is finishing—making the content move-in ready with good brand voice and curb appeal. Each stage builds on the previous one; without a strong foundation, nothing else matters.
real_qa.requete: message design content creation framework stages

real_qa.q: What is the Duncan Donuts tagline and what does it reveal about their core message?
real_qa.r: Duncan Donuts' tagline is 'America runs on Dunkin'', which reveals that their core message is that coffee is fuel. From 'runs on it,' you can infer that coffee must be fast and efficient. This deep-seated belief about coffee as fast fuel shows up throughout their entire brand experience, not just in the tagline, demonstrating how core message philosophy infects every customer touchpoint.
real_qa.requete: Dunkin Donuts America runs on tagline meaning

guest.bio_context: Tamsen Webster spent the first 15 years of her career working with nonprofits, including as Head of Marketing and Communications at Boston Conservatory (now part of Berklee College of Music). She has worked as a CMO and in agencies, and continues to work as an active content marketer herself while designing messages for B2B clients and startups.
